title: Planning Spring Landscaping Around Stumps That Need to Go First
meta_title: Planning Spring Landscaping Around Old Stumps
meta_description: If a stump sits where spring landscaping is planned, it needs to be handled first. Here's how to sequence a project that includes stump removal.
lede: A stump sitting exactly where a spring landscaping project is supposed to go has to be dealt with before anything else can start.
excerpt: Why stump removal needs to come first in a spring landscaping plan.

sections.heading: Grinding Disturbs the Site, So It Goes First
paragraphs: Grinding a stump and backfilling the hole disturbs the ground in that spot. Any planting, grading, or hardscaping planned for the same area needs that work finished first, not worked around afterward.

sections.heading: Backfilled Ground Needs Time to Settle
paragraphs: Topsoil backfill over a ground stump settles over time. Building a landscaping feature directly on top of freshly backfilled ground risks an uneven result once the soil has finished settling.

sections.heading: Winter Is a Good Time to Get the Stump Handled
paragraphs: Since spring is when landscaping projects actually get built, using the winter months to get any stumps ground and cleared means the site is ready to go once building season starts.

sections.heading: Planning the Whole Timeline
paragraphs: Getting a quote now for winter stump removal, with enough lead time before spring, keeps a landscaping project from being delayed by a stump that should have been handled months earlier.

faqs.q: Why can't a stump be ground at the same time as spring landscaping?
faqs.a: Grinding disturbs the site, so it needs to happen before other work in that area, not alongside it.

faqs.q: How much time should I leave between grinding and building on that spot?
faqs.a: Backfilled soil settles over time, so giving it time before building directly on top of it helps avoid an uneven result.

faqs.q: Is winter a good time to get ahead of a spring project like this?
faqs.a: Yes, using winter to grind and clear stumps means the site is ready once spring building season starts.
